Stage 3 runbook: Ship the order

No test of this runbook is on record.

Its alerts
Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's ageHow many paid orders are waiting to ship, and for how long? Escalation has gaps.No owner is named yet for: Fulfilment staff
The stage
Stage 3: Ship the orderits process steps, outcomes and measures
Shared by every alert
Before you start: the access you need

You need to be able to read each of these. A check you cannot run is a gap in this runbook: note it.

  • Order: Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age
  • Ordering API: Ordering API requests by route and status, and their duration; Ordering API transaction failures, by command
  • Ordering database: Ordering database accepting connections; Long-running statements on orderingdb; Connections to the postgres server against max_connections
  • Identity API: Identity API rate, errors, duration
  • Deployment, configuration and restart history for Ordering API, Catalog API, Webhooks API, Identity API.
Every check

Is Ordering API down or unreachable?

Used by Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's agePart Ordering APIReads Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age; Ordering API requests by route and status, and their duration
How to check
az containerapp replica list --name ordering-api --resource-group <rg> --query "[].properties.runningState"
Not the cause if at least one Running
The cause if none Running, or no replica
‹ Back to Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age
Ending Yes → Restore: remedy 14
Why this check reads it this way
The order stays Paid: nothing else moves it, because no timer watches Paid orders. Ordering API cannot be reached, so the ship call fails at the person's client

Is Ordering database down or unreachable?

Used by Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's agePart Ordering databaseReads Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age; Ordering database accepting connections
How to check

In the postgres container (az containerapp exec --name postgres --resource-group <rg>) run:

pg_isready -d orderingdb
Not the cause if accepting connections
The cause if no response, or rejecting connections
‹ Back to Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age
Ending Yes → Restore: remedy 14
Why this check reads it this way
The order stays Paid: nothing else moves it, because no timer watches Paid orders. The ordering database does not answer, so the ship command fails

Is Ordering API answering with errors?

Used by Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's agePart Ordering APIReads Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age; Ordering API requests by route and status, and their duration
How to check
Read M40 for the route PUT api/orders/ship over the window, by status
Not the cause if 200 only, or no calls
The cause if 400 or 500 answers
‹ Back to Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age
Ending Yes → Restore: remedy 14
Why this check reads it this way
The order stays Paid: nothing else moves it, because no timer watches Paid orders. Ordering API refuses the ship call: 400 when the x-requestid header is missing or empty, or 500 'Ship order failed to process.' when the command returns false

Is Ordering API slow to answer, or not answering at all?

Used by Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's agePart Ordering APIReads Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age; Ordering API requests by route and status, and their duration
How to check
Read M40 for the route PUT api/orders/ship over the window, its duration
Not the cause if calls answered within a few seconds
The cause if calls taking tens of seconds
‹ Back to Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age
Ending Yes → Can’t restore here: escalate to the owner of Ordering API
Why this check reads it this way
The ship call waits on Ordering API; the order ships when it answers, or the call ends and is made again

Is Ordering database slow?

Used by Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's agePart Ordering databaseReads Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age; Long-running statements on orderingdb
How to check

In the postgres container (az containerapp exec --name postgres --resource-group <rg>) run:

psql -U postgres -d orderingdb

Then:

SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = 'orderingdb' AND state = 'active' AND now() - query_start > interval '5 seconds';
Not the cause if 0
The cause if 1 or more, persisting
‹ Back to Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age
Ending Yes → Can’t restore here: escalate to the owner of Ordering database
Why this check reads it this way
Statements on the ordering database run long and the ship call answers late

Is Ordering database full or out of capacity?

Used by Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's agePart Ordering databaseReads Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age; Connections to the postgres server against max_connections
How to check

In the postgres container (az containerapp exec --name postgres --resource-group <rg>) run:

psql -U postgres -d orderingdb

Then:

SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;
SHOW max_connections;
Not the cause if well below max_connections
The cause if at max_connections
‹ Back to Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age
Ending Yes → Restore: remedy 14
Why this check reads it this way
The order stays Paid: nothing else moves it, because no timer watches Paid orders. The shared postgres server refuses new connections, so the ship command fails

Is the act failing inside Ordering API?

Used by Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's agePart Ordering APIReads Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age; Ordering API transaction failures, by command
How to check

Search the console log of ordering-api (az containerapp logs show --name ordering-api --resource-group <rg> --type console --tail 300 --format text (one replica per call; add --replica for the others)) for the 'Sending command:' lines whose OrderNumber is one of these orders, and after each for 'Handling command ShipOrderCommand' and 'Command ShipOrderCommand handled - response:'.

Not the cause if no ship command for the order (go on), or one handled with response true
The cause if a ship command for the order with no 'handled' line, or with response false
‹ Back to Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age
Ending Yes → Restore: remedy 14
Why this check reads it this way
The order stays Paid: nothing else moves it, because no timer watches Paid orders. The ship command fails: the order number is unknown, the order is not Paid so its setter throws, or the save throws; the identified-command handler swallows the exception into false

Has no Fulfilment staff acted on the cases?

Used by Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's agePart Fulfilment staffReads Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age
How to check

In the postgres container (az containerapp exec --name postgres --resource-group <rg>) run:

psql -U postgres -d orderingdb

Then:

SELECT "Id", "OrderDate" FROM ordering.orders WHERE "OrderStatus" = 'Paid' ORDER BY "OrderDate";

Ask whoever ships the goods which of them have left.

Not the cause if every listed order is still being prepared for dispatch
The cause if an order whose goods have left but which is still Paid, or one nobody is preparing
‹ Back to Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age
Ending Yes → Restore: remedy 14
Why this check reads it this way
The order stays Paid: nothing else moves it, because no timer watches Paid orders. Nobody records the shipment: nothing in the application calls the ship endpoint, so a person must call it with their own client, and no one is told an order is waiting (no caller in WebApp, ClientApp or any worker). This test lists the waiting orders; the tests before it say why a call that was made failed

Is Identity API down or unreachable?

Used by Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's agePart Identity APIReads Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age; Identity API rate, errors, duration
How to check
az containerapp replica list --name identity-api --resource-group <rg> --query "[].properties.runningState"
Not the cause if at least one Running
The cause if none Running, or no replica
‹ Back to Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age: Is Ordering API answering with errors? ‹ Back to Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age: Is Ordering API slow to answer, or not answering at all?
Ending Yes → Restore: remedy 14
Why this check reads it this way
The order stays Paid: nothing else moves it, because no timer watches Paid orders. Identity API does not answer: the person cannot get a token for the ship call, or Ordering API cannot fetch the keys to validate it, and the call is refused
Causes the design rules out, so no check is needed
  • Fulfilment staff, the person acts wrongly: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”): a wrong ship records Shipped and the order leaves the stage. A ship recorded before the goods left is the expected outcome “The order is shipped”'s wrong outcome, which no record counts (measure-gaps the expected outcome “The order is shipped”)
  • Fulfilment staff, caller gives up mid-call: as a cause apart from nobody recording the shipment: a call that ends early either shipped the order, which then leaves the stage, or did not, which leaves it Paid just as when no call is made, and the test of the waiting orders lists it (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”)
  • Ordering API, callee answers wrongly: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”): Ordering API answers 200 only after the command's save returned true
  • Ordering API, the act completes wrongly: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”): the setter acts only from Paid and writes only the status, its description and the shipped event
  • Ordering database, answers stale or wrong: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”): Ordering API reads the order from its one postgres server, with no replica
  • Identity API, slow: as a cause of its own: the keys are fetched by the JWT handler and kept, not on every call, so a slow Identity API delays only the token the person asks for. Counted by “Identity API rate, errors, duration”
  • Identity API, full or out of capacity: as a cause apart from Identity API not answering: a refusal shows on the same test and has the same effect. Counted by “Identity API rate, errors, duration”
  • Identity API, answers stale or wrong: as a cause apart from Identity API not answering: keys out of date make the ship call refused at authentication, as when it does not answer. Counted by “Ordering API requests by route and status, and their duration”
  • Ordering API, row left unpublished: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the order's status is already written with the event row. Here, the paid or shipped event row stays at State 0 or 1 and nothing sends it later. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”; Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Ordering API, publish marked failed: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the order's status is already written with the event row. Here, the row is set to 3 and never retried. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”; Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Ordering API, relay not running: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the order's status is already written with the event row. Here, there is no relay to stop: the request that committed the status change publishes right after its commit. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”; Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Ordering API, publish fails: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the stock reduction and the notifications do not touch the order. Here, Ordering API cannot hand the paid or shipped event to the broker; logged and the row marked failed. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”; Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Event bus, message not routed: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the stock reduction and the notifications do not touch the order. Here, no queue Catalog or Webhooks is bound for the event, so the broker drops it. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”; Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Catalog API and Webhooks API, consumer not running: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the stock reduction and the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the event waits in queue Catalog or Webhooks until its consumer returns. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”; Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Catalog API and Webhooks API, consumer fails on the message: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the stock reduction and the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the event is acknowledged and gone. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”; Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Catalog API and Webhooks API, consumer slow: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the stock reduction and the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the event is handled late. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”; Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Catalog API, the act fails: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), or of any change to the order: stock reduction does not touch the order. RemoveStock throws for an item already at zero and the save comes only after the loop, so none of the order's items is reduced. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”
  • Catalog API, the act completes wrongly: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), or of any change to the order: stock reduction does not touch the order. An item missing from the catalogue is skipped without a record: process step 3.1's wrong outcome, which no record counts (measure-gaps process step 3.1)
  • Webhook subscriber endpoint, callee down: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the subscriber's endpoint cannot be reached; the post is retried up to 3 times on a transient failure by the standard resilience handler, then throws out of the handler and the event is acknowledged and gone. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Webhook subscriber endpoint, callee returns an error: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the subscriber's error answer is not read, so nothing records it. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Webhook subscriber endpoint, callee slow or hangs: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the post waits on the subscriber, up to the resilience handler's timeout. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Webhooks API, caller gives up mid-call: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, a post that outlasts the resilience handler throws out of the handler, and the event is acknowledged and gone. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Webhook subscriber endpoint, callee answers wrongly: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the subscriber's answer is not read. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Ordering database, unavailable: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), or of any change to the order: the ordering database holds only the event row, written in the same transaction as the Paid status: if it fails, the order does not reach Paid, which the acceptance stage counts. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”
  • Ordering database, slow: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), or of any change to the order: the event row is written with the Paid status; a slow database delays reaching Paid, in the acceptance stage. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”
  • Ordering database, full or out of capacity: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), or of any change to the order: as when it does not answer: the order does not reach Paid. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”
  • Ordering database, answers stale or wrong: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), or of any change to the order: nothing here reads the database back; there is one server and no replica. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”
  • Catalog database, unavailable: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), or of any change to the order: stock reduction does not touch the order. Here, the catalog database does not answer, the stock reduction throws and the event is acknowledged and gone. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”
  • Catalog database, slow: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), or of any change to the order: stock reduction does not touch the order. Here, stock is reduced late. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”
  • Catalog database, full or out of capacity: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), or of any change to the order: stock reduction does not touch the order. Here, the shared postgres server refuses Catalog API's connections and the reduction fails as when it does not answer. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”
  • Catalog database, answers stale or wrong: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), or of any change to the order: stock reduction does not touch the order. Here, the stock figure read is reduced as found; there is one server and no replica. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”
  • Event bus, unavailable: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the broker does not answer and the publish of the paid or shipped event is marked failed, never re-sent. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”; Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Event bus, slow: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the event arrives late. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”; Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Event bus, full or out of capacity: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: a memory or disk alarm blocks the publish until it clears. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”; Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Event bus, answers stale or wrong: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the broker holds messages, not data the moves read. Stock left unreduced is counted per order by “Paid orders whose stock was not reduced”; Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Webhooks database, unavailable: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the webhooks database does not answer, the subscription read throws and the event is acknowledged and gone. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Webhooks database, slow: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the subscriptions are read late and subscribers told late. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Webhooks database, full or out of capacity: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the shared postgres server refuses Webhooks API's connections, and the read fails as when it does not answer. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Webhooks database, answers stale or wrong: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the subscriptions are read from one server with no replica. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Webhook subscriber endpoint, unavailable: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the subscriber's endpoint does not answer; the post is retried and then throws, and the event is acknowledged and gone for every subscriber. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Webhook subscriber endpoint, slow: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the subscriber answers late, holding the post up to the resilience handler's timeout. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Webhook subscriber endpoint, full or out of capacity: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the subscriber refuses the post, which is not read. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
  • Webhook subscriber endpoint, answers stale or wrong: as a cause of paid orders waiting to ship (“Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age”), of shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time (“Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the expected time”), or of any change to the order: the notifications do not touch the order. Here, the subscriber's answer is not read. Subscribers not told are counted per order by “Paid orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (paid) and “Shipped orders whose webhook subscribers were not posted” (shipped)
Restore

After any action that restores: go back to the entry of the alert that fired and run its checks again for every case still affected, since a restore can leave cases in other states.

Remedy 14: re-drive

First clear the cause the test found (its part restored, or its owner engaged). Then have whoever ships the goods confirm which of the listed Paid orders have left, and record each by PUT /api/orders/ship on ordering-api, with a new GUID in the x-requestid header, the person's bearer token and the body {"orderNumber": <id>}
Expected 200 for each, and its "OrderStatus" reads 'Shipped'; the count of paid orders waiting falls
If different A 500 'Ship order failed to process.' for an order that is Paid: Escalate

Declare an incident when the operators’ severity definition says to: the register holds no trigger for it. Keep working the entry while it is declared. For that call, what is at stake here is below; the stage itself is Stage 3: Ship the order.

What is at stake.

  • Order id ("Id"): The only key that joins the order across services and to the customer
  • Order total (sum of Units x UnitPrice): Money the customer pays; value blocked while the order is stuck
  • Items and units (ordering."orderItems"): What must be in stock and shipped
  • Buyer (ordering.buyers "IdentityGuid"): Who is waiting and who is told
  • Delivery address: Where the goods must arrive
  • Payment method (card number masked to the last four digits): What is charged
  • Cannot be undone: The order is shipped
  • Manual rework and absorbed cost, if “Stock is reduced by the order's units” fails: counted in paid orders whose stock was not reduced. Later stock checks confirm against stock already sold
  • Customer experience and trust, if “Webhook subscribers are told the order is paid” fails: counted in paid orders whose subscribers were not told. Retried up to 3 times on a transient failure by the standard resilience handler, then not sent again; response not read
  • Customer experience and trust, if “The order is shipped” fails: counted in paid orders waiting to ship. Nothing moves a Paid order but a person's call

What to hand over: the alert and what it guards (its entry); the affected case ids by state; whether new cases are still affected now; which checks ran and what they showed; what was contained and what was done; the look-back time.

EndingClose

Self-healedOnly for an alert that counts cases waiting: confirm it is back under its threshold, then close. Note that its threshold or window may be wrong.
RestoreAfter the action, confirm the alert is under its threshold, no case it counted is still affected, and new cases get through. Any that remain: back to its entry.

Stage 3 runbook: Ship the order › Alert

Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age

No test of this runbook is on record.

A paid order still waiting has not been shipped when the customer expects the goods, and nothing moves it but a person recording the shipment: no timer watches Paid orders and nothing in the application calls the ship endpoint (lifecycle “The order is shipped”, recovery stranded).

How long a wait is too long is the operators' dispatch target, not the register's.

This measure is not emitted yet; deployed as written, the alert fires on No data until it is. If it shows No data rather than a count, that is why: it counts no case, so there is nothing to work here; note it for the hand-over and close.

It has been above the operators’ threshold for longer than their window (the alert).

Its cases those held in the stage past the time limit. A case not past the time limit is not one of this alert's.
Look back from when the oldest of its cases entered the stage, to now. The alert fires only once a case has waited past the time limit, so its cause can be as old as that: never read a test over only the time since the count began rising.
Do now
  1. List its cases and set the look-back. Every check below runs on these cases, over that time. List them with the alert’s own count:
    How

    Rows in 'Paid'; age from the order's OrderStatusChangedToPaid outbox row "CreationTime"

  2. Contain. No hold is needed: the cases the alert counts are still in the stage, and nothing more is done to them while they wait.
  3. Do not: the register names no action to avoid here.
  4. Escalate or declare as soon as a trigger is met, at any point below. Triggers ›
Check first
1Is this already known?
How
Look for an open incident, or a known error with a fix in flight, for any of these parts: Ordering API, Catalog API, Ordering database, Catalog database, Event bus, Webhooks API, Webhooks database, Webhook subscriber endpoint, Identity API. Not the cause if there is none; the cause if one is open: link it and close.
Yes → Already known
2Was it planned?
How
Look for a maintenance window on any of those parts, or a planned change to a timing the stage depends on (Process step 3.1: Stock is reduced by the order's units — No timeout: the stock is reduced when Catalog API consumes the Paid event from queue Catalog; no clock watches the message waiting there, and the queue sets no expiry; Process step 3.2: Webhook subscribers are told the order is paid — Each post is bounded only by the standard resilience handler every HTTP client carries: each attempt 10 seconds, up to 3 retries, 30 seconds in all; the posts to all subscriptions go out together and are awaited together. No clock watches the message waiting in queue Webhooks; Expected outcome: The order is shipped — No timeout: a person ships the goods and records it, and nothing in the application schedules or times that act). Not the cause if there is none; the cause if a window is open or a setting was changed on purpose: link it and close.
Yes → Planned change
3Did something change when it started?
How
Look for any deploy, configuration change or unplanned restart of those parts since the look-back time above. Not the cause if there is none; the cause if a change lines up with the start.
Yes → Roll the change back, or escalate to the owner of the part that changed
4Is it already recovering?
How
Read the alert's own count over one window (for a count of cases waiting, with the oldest only just past the time limit). Not the cause if it is not falling; it is recovering if the count falls within one window: confirm it is back under its threshold, then close.
Yes → Self-healed
Find the cause in order, on its cases only. No → next check. Yes → take its ending for the cases it lists, and go on for the rest. A check whose evidence lists no cases (a match in a log or a metric) explains no case by itself: note it, if the match falls inside the look-back, and go on; a case no later check explains takes the ending of every check noted for it, each named in the hand-over; where those endings differ, escalate rather than restore. A result you cannot read, or a check you cannot run: note it for the hand-over and go on. Where a command asks for a time span in angle brackets, give it the look-back above; where it asks for case ids in angle brackets, give it the ids of the cases you are working. Where a command reads only the last lines of a log (--tail), a line not found there rules its cause out only if the oldest line returned is older than the look-back time; if it is not, note the check for the hand-over as not fully run, and go on.

How
How to check
az containerapp replica list --name ordering-api --resource-group <rg> --query "[].properties.runningState"
Not the cause if at least one Running

How
How to check

pg_isready -d orderingdb
Not the cause if accepting connections
The cause if no response, or rejecting connections

Yes → Restore: remedy 14

How
How to check

If yes, also check, on the same cases: Is Identity API down or unreachable?

5Is Ordering database slow?
How
How to check

In the postgres container (az containerapp exec --name postgres --resource-group <rg>) run:

psql -U postgres -d orderingdb

Then:

SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = 'orderingdb' AND state = 'active' AND now() - query_start > interval '5 seconds';
Not the cause if 0
The cause if 1 or more, persisting
The same check in the reference ›
Yes → Can’t restore here: escalate to the owner of Ordering database
6Is Ordering database full or out of capacity?
How
How to check

In the postgres container (az containerapp exec --name postgres --resource-group <rg>) run:

psql -U postgres -d orderingdb

Then:

SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;
SHOW max_connections;
Not the cause if well below max_connections
The cause if at max_connections
The same check in the reference ›
Yes → Restore: remedy 14
7Is the act failing inside Ordering API?
How
How to check

Search the console log of ordering-api (az containerapp logs show --name ordering-api --resource-group <rg> --type console --tail 300 --format text (one replica per call; add --replica for the others)) for the 'Sending command:' lines whose OrderNumber is one of these orders, and after each for 'Handling command ShipOrderCommand' and 'Command ShipOrderCommand handled - response:'.

Not the cause if no ship command for the order (go on), or one handled with response true
The cause if a ship command for the order with no 'handled' line, or with response false
The same check in the reference ›
Yes → Restore: remedy 14
8Has no Fulfilment staff acted on the cases?
How
How to check

In the postgres container (az containerapp exec --name postgres --resource-group <rg>) run:

psql -U postgres -d orderingdb

Then:

SELECT "Id", "OrderDate" FROM ordering.orders WHERE "OrderStatus" = 'Paid' ORDER BY "OrderDate";

Ask whoever ships the goods which of them have left.

Not the cause if every listed order is still being prepared for dispatch
The cause if an order whose goods have left but which is still Paid, or one nobody is preparing
